extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, academic researchers, journalists, and organizations interested in news trust and democracy
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of a multiyear research initiative (Knight + Gallup, 2017–2022) examining American attitudes about trust in journalism, the financial sustainability of news, and technology/internet policy as they relate to news and democracy. The page presents themes, goals, and indicators of impact for the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependable, academic-quality research
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to provide dependable, academic-quality research to inform a nationwide conversation on news and democracy in America (multiyear initiative, 2017–2022, in partnership with Gallup).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should be rigorous and suitable for academic and policy audiences; produce survey data and analyses that can inform public discussion and policymaking. (Page emphasizes that the initiative was established to examine causes and consequences of declining trust in journalism and to provide dependable research.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme 1 — Trust, Media and Democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyzes American attitudes toward trust, media and democracy since 2017. While a majority of Americans acknowledge the news media's crucial role in democracy, they believe it falls short due to perceived inaccuracy and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work under this theme should document attitudes about media credibility, perceived bias and accuracy, and track changes over time since 2017.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme 2 — The Financial Sustainability of News
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates Americans' willingness to pay for news and their attitudes toward the financial state and funding models of news organizations. The analyses underscore a persistent market failure — many individuals recognize the benefit of the news to the public but are unwilling to pay for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research should assess payment willingness, perceptions of funding models, and implications of market failures for news viability and public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme 3 — Attitudes About the Internet and Technology Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigates American attitudes toward regulation issues at the intersection of media and technology. The analysis identifies six distinct segments, not defined by political partisanship, of American views on internet regulation, which have important implications for policymakers, industry leaders, journalists and scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyses should segment public opinion on internet regulation and explore implications for policy and industry; segmentation should not assume alignment with partisan identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and impact goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary goal is to disseminate the most compelling findings, offer critical reflections and share survey data resulting from the partnership; through these efforts, the initiative aims to raise public awareness, foster understanding and catalyze actions that address critical issues on news consumption and trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expected outputs include public reporting of findings, critical commentary, release of survey datasets, and outreach intended to influence public understanding and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about research limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Within each theme, the initiative provides insights into the broader research landscape, highlights key discoveries and identifies any research limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research products should explicitly acknowledge limitations and contextualize findings within the broader literature and methodological constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement and impact indicators (policy & academia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicators of the initiative's impact include citation in congressional hearings, reports and bill filings (public policy); high engagement from academic audiences, citation in more than 500 academic publications including leading journals, references in white papers from Brookings, Aspen, Carnegie Endowment, and citation in books used in college classrooms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use policy citations, academic citations, inclusion in curricula, references in influential white papers, and private briefings as measurable evidence of research influence and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement (private briefings and targeted outreach)
rubrics_metrics.description: The partnership conducted private briefings for academics and engaged policy and academic audiences through publications and events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure and foster targeted engagement (e.g., briefings, events) with key stakeholder groups to amplify research uptake among scholars and policymakers.
